subject: Clarifying incident notice parameters, jurisdictional handover & subprocessor roles
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: clarification on FinEdge ask — quick internal alignment

Marissa / Ben,

FinEdge just surfaced two items we need to answer together before legal signs: 1) their requirement for a ‘jurisdictional handover’ clause describing when and how we hand evidence to a customer or a regulator (they called it an "escrow-lite" path), and 2) a question about timelines — they want to know if we can commit to a 24-hour initial notification for incidents involving EU customer data, but allow for exceptions when evidence collection requires cross-border work.

High-level thoughts:
- Our baseline DPA incident notice says "without undue delay" and we currently aim for 48 hours for initial customer-facing notification for sensitive incidents.
- We can offer a 24-hour notification for verified data exfil and PII exposure only if the customer accepts a narrowly scoped exception for forensic evidence retention and cross-border export (i.e., we may need an additional 72–120 hour window to preserve/transfer raw forensic artifacts).
- Subprocessor coordination: we need to be explicit about who is responsible for producing logs/telemetry and timelines for subproc suppliers (e.g., GPU hosters, telemetry pipeline). Recommend enumerating subproc classes and a 3-tier SLA: (1) telemetry snapshot (48h), (2) full export (up to 7 days with notice), (3) legal transfer (subject to lawful transfer / export controls).

Questions I have for you both:
1) Legal acceptability — is the 24h-with-exception approach something we can put in a customer-facing DPA redline?
2) Ops feasibility — can Ben’s team guarantee a telemetry snapshot (redacted) within 48h for EU tenants, and what exceptions do we need for cross-border work?
3) Messaging — we should propose explicit cooperation steps: initial acknowledgement, interim summary, evidence handover plan, and final closure. Attach two drafts: my clause proposal and the evidence handover matrix.

I attached a draft clause and a matrix for reference. I’ll call FinEdge after we have a short Q/A to avoid ping-pong.

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Redwood proposal: incident notice windows, handover steps & subprocessor responsibilities

Hi Ana / Lukas,

Thanks for the detailed note earlier today. We reviewed your ask and wanted to propose a concise set of parameters so your legal & infosec teams can validate quickly. Below is our proposed language and operational commitments; we’ve attached a redline and a one-page handover matrix for clarity.

Proposal (high level):
1) Initial notification: Redwood will provide customers an initial written notification for security incidents affecting customer data within 24 hours of confirming a material impact to that customer's data subjects, limited to incidents that meet the DPA-defined exposure thresholds (unauthorized access, exfiltration, or PII exposure).
2) Evidence collection window: For forensic collection and custodial transfers of raw logs or disk artifacts, Redwood reserves a limited evidence preservation window of up to 120 hours from initial notification to enable secure collection, legal review, and lawful transfer steps when cross-border export controls or subprocessor cooperation apply. We will disclose the need for any additional time in the initial notification and provide periodic updates.
3) Subprocessor roles: Redwood will identify the class of subprocessor responsible for primary telemetry (telemetry providers), model serving (GPU hosters), and logging/observability (log storage providers). For each class Redwood will: a) provide a snapshot of telemetry (redacted where necessary) within 48 hours where feasible; b) initiate a full export within 72 hours where the subprocessor permits; c) escalate to legal ops if export is delayed due to export controls or third-party approvals.
4) Jurisdictional handover & escrow-lite: When a customer or regulator requires direct access to preserved artifacts, Redwood will coordinate a secure handover to a mutually agreed custodian (customer-managed S3, secure courier of physical media under chain-of-custody, or using an escrow partner). Redwood will not unilaterally transfer customer data to a regulator without court order but will cooperate and provide documented artifacts under lawful process.

Operational caveats (for transparency):
- Cross-border transfers may require redaction, tokenization, or an intermediary transfer via our internal EU-only evidence staging environment.
- When subprocessor contracts or local law prevent immediate exports, Redwood will provide detailed technical proofs (hashes, indexes, metadata) and an executed plan to enable customer/regulator review.

Please see attached: Redwood_DPA_incident_clause_proposal-v3.docx (redline) and evidence-handover-matrix.xlsx.

If this high-level approach works, we can formalize the clause in a narrow DPA addendum that applies only to incidents and lists the exact incident thresholds. Happy to jump on a call today if you prefer.

Best,
Hannah

From: Ana Kovac <legal@finedge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Security - FinEdge <security@finedge.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 07:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal: incident notice windows, handover steps & subprocessor responsibilities

Hannah —

Thanks for the thoughtful proposal and for surfacing operational caveats. A few clarifying points from our side so our internal counsel and incident team can sign off:

1) 24-hour initial notification: we appreciate the carve for "DPA-defined exposure thresholds". Please confirm whether the 24h commitment applies to "initial acknowledgement" (we are ok with a short-form acknowledgement) or to a substantive incident summary that includes scope & affected tenant identifiers.

2) Evidence preservation window (up to 120 hours): we need an explicit guarantee that during that period Redwood will not delete or overwrite primary artifacts, and will provide a cryptographic hash for each preserved object within 48 hours of preservation.

3) Subprocessor SLAs: the classes make sense; can you provide a sample escalation timeline that maps to the following: Snapshot (48h), Export initiation (72h), Export completion target (7 days) and an exception pathway document if the subprocessor refuses export? We will need that documented as part of our procurement checklist.

4) Jurisdictional handover: we prefer a default of customer-managed escrow (customer S3 encrypted to customer key). If Redwood proposes to use an escrow partner, please include the partner name and data handling controls. Also we need assurance that Redwood will not be the data controller for any artifacts transferred to a regulator — i.e., Redwood assists but does not assert ownership.

A couple of practical asks:
- Please add a short clause addressing law enforcement/regulatory requests (a template of how Redwood will respond and timelines for Redwood to notify FinEdge unless prohibited).
- Can you replace the term "escrow-lite" in the redline with "custodial handover"? Our legal ops has concerns about the word "escrow" implying third-party custody by default.

If you can incorporate these items into v4 of the redline, we can fast-track to signature. Otherwise we are likely to request a narrow amendment during contracting.

Regards,
Ana Kovac
Senior Counsel, FinEdge

--
Ana Kovac
Legal Department
FinEdge
